text.p: Tropical Storm Yates is rapidly intensifying over the western Pacific and may pose a threat to the northern Mariana Islands. Yates, with 65 mph winds, is centered near 16n/156e and moving west northwest at 17 mph. Top winds are expected to reach 100 mph or more within 48 hours, when the storm will be nearing the northern Mariana Islands from the east southeast. Yates will become a major threat to shipping in the region.

The extratropical remains of Typhoon Violet, with top winds still near 75 mph, continue to race north northeastward in the waters northeast of Japan. The center of the storm was near 43n/148e in the latest report. By 36 hours, the center should be near 50n/159e, with top winds of 60 mph. This storm system will be a threat to shipping out over the northwestern Pacific.

Tropical Depression Willie has a poorly defined center and is dissipating over northern Vietnam and northern Laos. The leftover tropical moisture from this system will drift west southwestward across Indochina during the next 24-48 hours, bringing heavy rainfall and fairly widespread flooding to the region. Mudslides are likely in the more hilly terrain.
